SF DEATH FOG · v3 · CLOUD PIPELINE

Fog Pipeline Atlas

How the fog on the map is made: geometry and wind are simulated once on a GPU, then every ~30 minutes a GitHub Action blends forecasts, stations and satellite into fog tops, street wetness and 3D fog, which the browser draws. Every figure is real output: the beta build of 2026-11-18 04:43 UTC (17 Nov, 20:43 PT), the offline libraries on the PC, and branch v3-dev. Crops are shown inside their source with a red box.

855 × 811 × 4020 m cells in the city grid
15wind directions simulated
11fog inflow bands per direction
285,809street points simulated
144 sone beta build

Click a box to jump to its stage. Each stage lists its input, its output, the variables you can change (and the matching cloud-menu control, if any), and its third-party sources.

Wind tiers: where each gets its input

There is no single wind model. Each tier below takes its input from a different place; only the 20 m and 5 m tiers are real flow simulations.

Where the code and the guides disagree

The code is the source of truth. These are places where a guide, the README or a config file says something the running code or data does not.

  1. Wind solver walls. v3-dev wind.py lacks the walls fix and free-slip sea. The beta library was built from branch wind-cube-check. 00_README's "Guide 01 needs no new wind runs" is out of date. Near-surface ratio at 270°: old 1.007 median, walls 0.377.
  2. Tracer diffusivity. Beta tracer assets use kd 20 and kdv 8 from spike scripts. microclimate.toml still says eddy_diffusivity_m2s = 2.0 and has no vertical key.
  3. 5 m correction. README says the 297-patch correction is used. True for public (rel_wind median 0.498); the beta static has rel_wind = 1 everywhere, because the correction was computed on the no-walls field.
  4. TRACER_REF. 0.03 was tuned on the old tracer. The beta point tracer at 270° is p5 0.18 / p50 0.27 / p95 0.46, so almost every point saturates. Public: p5 0.001, p50 0.12, p95 0.54.
  5. fog5 tiles vs hourly tiles. fog5 tiles are 255 · A · trb with no cloud base; the beta hourly tile uses tile_from_3d with the base. At 03 UTC the hourly tile is empty while fog5 shows fog. (fog5 volumes do use base and lid.)
  6. Switch table. fog_lid, fog_base_2d and tile_from_3d (16 Nov) are missing from 00_README's switch table.
  7. Sky lab hint. The lab hint and a fog2.js comment say "nothing is drawn" for sky, but macro.js does draw the deck (kept above the fog top).
  8. fog5 wind. status.json says "uniform (fogflow.js wind not used yet)"; guide 08 plans terrain-aware wind.
  9. Fog-top cap. wetness FOG_TOP_MAX is 900 m, the forcing cap is 1300 m.
  10. Directions. microclimate.toml lists 202.5–360°; the assets also carry 180° and the six east directions.

A · Offline: simulated once on the PC

A1

City geometry: terrain and buildings on a 20 m grid

microclimate/geometry.py → solid_20m.npz · offline, PC, once

Terrain from USGS 3DEP and building footprints from DataSF are burned into a voxel grid of 855 × 811 × 40 cells, 20 m on each side, starting at UTM 10N x0 = 540100, y0 = 4171500 (i = east, j = north, cell centres at z = (k + 0.5) · 20 m above sea level). A cell is solid if the ground or a building's mean height reaches it. This run: 177,023 buildings, highest roof 218 m, terrain max 372 m, solid fraction 0.042.

A2

Wind library: 20 m city LBM, 15 directions

microclimate/wind.py, windrot.py → wind_<dir>.npz → live_static / live_east.npz · offline, PC GPU (RTX 4080 SUPER)

XLB solves the flow over solid_20m with a D3Q19 lattice Boltzmann scheme and a Smagorinsky closure, once per wind direction, with a uniform inflow of U_LAT = 0.05 lattice units. Each run is done in a rotated frame (the grid is resampled so the wind blows along x, then the field is rotated back), and the result is stored as speed divided by inflow speed, so one run serves every wind speed. The live build later multiplies by the forecast wind and blends the two nearest directions.

Directions: nine westerly (180–360° every 22.5°) and six easterly (22.5–135°). 157.5° is a known gap. Easterly fields are street wind only: their tracer rows are zero (status.json: "east tracer rows are zero").

This direction (270°): 40,000 steps in 435 s, max ratio 1.38, density 0.92–1.08. Near-surface ratio p5/p50/p95 = 0.06 / 0.38 / 1.04. The library made before 16 Nov had 0.995 / 1.007 / 1.018: a stale GPU kernel cache meant it ran with no walls at all.

A3

Nested refinement: 5 m patches and a 2.5 m Potrero run

refine.py (branch v3-refine) → patch_corr_2700.npz, patch_corr_2700_dx2p5.npz · offline, PC GPU, 270° only

297 patches of the city are re-run at 5 m with real building shapes. Each patch takes its boundary from the 20 m field (one-way nesting with a sponge), and the result is a correction corr_bldg = street speed with buildings ÷ without. This run: 297 patches, 251,061 street cells, corr p5/p50/p95 = 0.03 / 0.33 / 1.01. A 2.5 m Potrero patch exists and wins where it has a value. The wetness uses rel_wind = clip(corr / 0.91, 0.25, 1).

Guide 12's street5m_v2 spike is a separate, un-nested 5 m run with uniform inflow (go on the physics, with conditions). Note: the corrections were computed on the no-walls 20 m field, so they are stale for the beta library (see Disagreements).

A4

Fog tracer: 11 inflow bands per direction

microclimate/fog.py → fog_<dir>_<band>.npz → live_tracer3d.npz · offline, PC GPU

For each direction and each inflow height band, a steady advection–diffusion tracer is run through the wind field: concentration 1 enters at the west edge in that band, ground cells lose it by deposition. The live build later decides how much fog is in each band (from the fog top) and adds the bands up. Band edges (m): 0, 40, 100, 140, 200, 260, 300, 360, 420, 500, 640, 800. The old four bands are exact sums: 0–2, 3–5, 6–8, 9–10.

270°, three bands: about 11,000 steps of 1 s, 17 s each, drift over the last 2000 steps ≤ 0.006.

B · Live build: every ~30 minutes

B1

Gather: every live input

live/build.py, fetch.py, stations.py · GitHub Action, every ~30 min

One run pulls the RRFS forecast on a 6 × 5 lattice (37.70–37.83 N, 122.52–122.35 W) from Open-Meteo, plus CO-OPS, METARs, NWS, the Oakland sounding, 21 stations and GOES. Lattice points west of x = 545000 form the coast series s(t). Snapshot run 2026-11-18T04:43:58 Z: sources used coops, goes, goes_dsr, metar, nws, rrfs, sounding, stations; none failed; 21 of 24 stations reporting; sounding valid 2026-11-18T00:00 Z with 172 levels.

B2

GOES ingest: clear-sky mask and cloud-top height

live/goes.py, goes5.py → state/goes5/<date>/<hh>.npz · every run; 5-minute scans

Each CONUS scan (2500 × 1500 px) is cropped to goes.BOX = (−123.3, 37.2, −121.9, 38.3), which is 74 × 51 px around the Bay. ACM (clear-sky mask) and ACHA (cloud-top height) scans are paired within 60 s. Rule v1 turns them into p = low-cloud probability (cloudy with top below 1000 m) and c = confidence (1 by day, 0.7 by night, 0 within ±6° of sunrise/sunset). High cloud above a pixel makes it unscorable.

B3

Forcing: fog source s(t), nudging and station anchors

live/forcing.py, anchors.py · every run

The coast series gives a model fog source smodel(t) from RRFS low cloud. Where GOES and the KHAF ceiling observe it, sused = 0.5 · smodel + 0.5 · sobs, and the correction fades into the forecast with a 3 h e-folding time (wind and temperature: 6 h). The station fit (anchors FTPC1, GGBC1, PXOC1) corrects wind speed and direction. This run: 10 observed hours, mean s model 0.39, wind ratio at the last nudged hour 0.5, direction offset 45°.

B4

Fog top: fusion of model, GOES, ceilings and the sounding

live/topfusion.py (C.BETA top_fusion), fogtop.py · every run

A Kalman filter with a Rauch–Tung–Striebel backward pass. The model humidity profile gives a top every hour (σ 120 m, 250 m when it hits a floor or cap); GOES gives the low-cloud top over Ocean Beach (σ 250 m); a ceiling plus 250 m of stratus is an observation (σ 120 m); the sounding inversion (σ 50 m + 30 m per hour away). Observations more than 3 σ from the state are skipped. This run: model 78 used / 1 rejected, GOES 7 used, sounding 14 rejected (inversion base 2486 m, far above the fog).

B5

Wetness simulation at every street point

microclimate/wetness.py simulate() · every run, 10 min steps, 60 min output

Each of the street points gets its own fog arrival (tracer × fog source, lagged by travel time at 1.3 × wind), drizzle, rain, in-place fog, sun on a water film and pavement heat. W is an index from 0 to 100 (the index says: "hand-set constants (not calibrated): an index, not a measurement"). This run: 79 hourly frames, 92,429 columns; mean W saturates near 100 from frame 16 when rain of 2–6 mm/h arrives.

B7

3D fog volume, cloud base and lid

live/fog3d.py, fogbase.py, outputs.py write_fog3d() → fog3d_NNN.png · every run

vol = amp · Σd wd Σb ab tr3d / 255 · weight3d, where ab is how much of band b lies under the fused top. The base is zm + 125 · (T − Td) + offset (the urban lift over warm, calm, built-up ground is off); a strong column keeps at least 30 m of fog under its top; the lid fades from top + 50 m to top + 150 m. 24 levels of 25 m are packed into a 6 × 4 atlas PNG; the viewer reads value 16 as full density. Frame 12 (00:00 PT 18 Nov): top 134 m, σ 103 m, base 104 m, max value 156.

Cloud score: does the model match the satellite?

live/cloud_score.py → cloud_score.json · every run

Each hour and box is a yes/no for low cloud at 0.5. Fields scored: rrfs, source, fog_sheet, fog_sheet_nosat. Headline: Cloud match, last 24 h: 78 % (23 scorable hours). That headline field is nudged with the same satellite it is scored against, so it measures consistency, not skill (cloud_score.json says so). The independent RRFS score over 24 h: day CSI 0.182, night CSI 0.08 (hit rate 0.132).

B11

Sky layers and publishing

live/skylayers.py; build.py writes status.json, index.json · every run

Up to three cloud layers per hour above the fog from the RRFS humidity profile, METAR layers and the satellite top (guide 13). Then everything is written and deployed by GitHub Actions to Pages. This beta run took 143.9 s (94.1 s of simulation) and wrote 3D atlases of 4.4 MB.

C · Viewer: in the browser

C1

Viewer: voxel fog and the cloud menu

site/v3/fog2.js, foglab.js, fog3dview.js · in the browser

The 3D atlas becomes a WebGL 3D texture that is ray-marched over the terrain. The fog top shape, softness, detail, billows and light are drawn here, not computed in the build. The cloud menu opens with ?lab=1.
